reviewer: AI (Claude) independent reviewers (blind solve + informed review), separate from the author; not a native-speaker or teacher review

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A family moves to a new home because of heavy rain.
A mother teaches her sons how to cook a big dinner.
Two children make a rainy day fun with boxes.
A father repairs the roof while his children sleep.
qs.why: 비 오는 날 지루해하던 두 아이가 상자로 성을 만들며 즐겁게 보낸다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: Why was the narrator's little brother bored?
o: He had to stay in because of the rain.
He was sick and needed to see a doctor.
His mother did not let him use the sofa.
He had already finished building his toys.
qs.why: 비 오는 토요일이라 밖에 나가 놀 수 없어서 지루해했다고 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: Where did the narrator find the boxes?
qs.why: 본문에서 'old boxes stored under the stairs'라고 했어요.

qs.q: How did Mom probably feel at the end of the story?
o: Angry about the mess in the room
Bored with the castle after a while
Pleased and ready to join the fun
qs.why: 놀라워하며 미소 짓고 함께했다는 표현에서 기뻐했음을 알 수 있어요.

patches.why: q1 해설의 "남매"는 근거 없는 추정(두 형제일 수도 있음)

qs.q: What did the writer of the letter ask the reader to do?
qs.why: 편지에 'please plant a tree for me'라고 쓰여 있었어요.

o: She had written the letter herself long ago.
She wanted Hana to leave the library quickly.
The idea fit the school's garden plans.
She thought the paper looked very expensive.
qs.why: 정원에 나무가 더 필요하다는 말에서 편지의 부탁이 마침 학교 사정과 맞았다고 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, the word “faded” is closest in meaning to ____.
qs.why: faded는 색이나 글씨가 흐릿해진 상태를 뜻해요.

qs.q: What does “it” refer to in the last sentence?
qs.why: 앞에서 편지를 액자에 넣어 벽에 걸었다고 했으므로 방문객이 읽을 수 있는 것은 편지예요.

patches.why: faded q3 key was the only longer option (17 vs 13); lengthened distractors

qs.q: How did the dog react to the robot vacuum at first?
o: He barked and chased it outside.
He hid because he was scared.
He jumped on top of it happily.
He ignored it and kept sleeping.
qs.why: 처음에는 겁을 먹고 침대 밑에 숨었다고 했어요.

qs.q: What does “it” in “we have to rescue it” refer to?
qs.why: 소파 밑에 끼는 것은 로봇 청소기예요.

qs.q: What can we guess about the brother?
o: He expects the robot to fix his mess.
He wants to sell the robot to a neighbor.
He is afraid of the dog and the machine.
He cleans the whole house every day.
qs.why: 양말을 아무 데나 두고 로봇이 해결할 거라고 말하는 모습에서 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: What is the writer's attitude toward the robot vacuum?
qs.why: 장점을 인정하면서도 재미있게 단점을 말하고 있어요.

patches.why: q2 and q4 keys were far longer than distractors (16 vs 7-9; 32 vs 17-20)

qs.q: What did Grandfather teach the writer to do?
o: Sell fresh tomatoes at a local store
Build a small wooden house for birds
Pick wild flowers for a big vase
Tie climbing beans to wooden sticks
qs.why: 본문에서 콩 줄기를 나무 막대에 묶는 법을 가르쳤다고 했어요.

qs.q: How did the writer's feeling change?
qs.why: 처음에는 지루했지만 점차 흥미를 느꼈다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why does Grandfather probably smile so much while working?
o: He is waiting for visitors to arrive.
He has just won a gardening prize.
He plans to move to a bigger house.
qs.why: 직접 기른 채소로 샐러드를 먹은 뒤 이유를 이해했다는 흐름에서 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, “patience” is closest in meaning to ____.
qs.why: patience는 서두르지 않고 차분히 기다리는 태도를 뜻해요.

patches.why: patience q4 key uniquely longest (26 vs 13-18)

set.ex: The museum has a fascinating exhibit about ancient ships.
set.exko: 그 박물관에는 고대 선박에 관한 아주 흥미로운 전시가 있어요.

patches.why: ko 매력적인 means attractive/charming, not fascinating; 매력적인 전시 is awkward. Gloss changed to 아주 흥미로운 (en unchanged); charming added to syn.
"She was hungry to win first prize" is a natural idiom (hungry to win), a second reading in the cloze; replaced hungry

criteria: single defensible answer (blind solve), natural English, level, distractor validity, hint and explanation
